h.strategy: Propose hypotheses where the condition plausibly changes the edit's effect by a large amount through a simple mechanism: redundancy (an alternative path or component already provides what the edit adds), disconnection (the edited part cannot influence the outcome under the condition), saturation (gains shrink when capacity is already high), or bottleneck (gains grow when the edited part is the limiting factor). Make sure the direction follows unambiguously from the mechanism. Avoid conditions unrelated to the edited part.

hyps.why: With the direct 0->3 path removed, edge 5 is a more limiting route to the output, so a conv there gains more.
A skip on the parallel direct path already provides an identity/gradient route into node 3, making extra conv capacity on edge 4 partly redundant.
With edge 1 removed, edge 2 is the only route into node 2, so a conv there gains more.
Node 2 already receives strong conv features through edge 1, so extra conv capacity on edge 2 is saturated.
A skip direct path buffers the loss of the 2->3 route, so removing edge 5 is less harmful.
Without edge 2, edge 5 is the sole processing after the 0->2 hop, so a conv there gains more.
Conv-rich indirect paths already supply capacity into node 3, so a conv on the direct edge is redundant.
With edge 2 removed, edge 1 is the sole way into node 2, so a conv there gains more.
A conv on edge 0 is only useful if node 1's features are consumed downstream, which a strong conv on edge 4 ensures.
Replacing a skip on the direct path discards a strong residual route, so the conv gains less than when filling an empty or weak slot.
